nodes.label: rig_deck Deterministic-Deck Test Pattern
nodes.rationale: Random-deck smoke tests cannot assert pot distributions because cards aren't deterministic. The rig_deck helper pre-sets hole cards and replaces table.deck with a fixed sequence driving burn/flop/turn/river, enabling exact final-stack assertions. Rule: distribution semantics need engineered decks; random decks belong only in completion/panic tests.

nodes.label: Chip Conservation Is Necessary But Insufficient
nodes.rationale: Chip-conservation audits (table_chip_count == sum of starting stacks) only verify no chips were created or destroyed; chips can be conserved while routed to the wrong winner (42,445 in, 42,445 out, but split 21,222/21,223 instead of 34,985/7,460). Pot-resolution tests must assert who got the chips per seat, not just aggregate conservation.

nodes.label: Twin Implementations Are a Bug Multiplier
nodes.rationale: TableNoCell::showdown_multiway and the cell-based Showdown::process_multiway implement the same algorithm; the ==-instead-of->= bug existed line-for-line in both because they were authored as twins. Fixes and tests in one don't cover the other. Rule: when fixing a bug in TableNoCell or TableCelled, immediately check the twin file for the same code shape.

nodes.label: Event-Log Shape Is a Public API
nodes.rationale: Changing which TableAction variant end_hand emits (PlayerWins vs PlayerWinsMainPot/SidePot) is a behavior change visible to every downstream event-log consumer (pkdealer, pkarena0-web, pkpy, pknotebook). The asymmetric-only delegate was chosen over always routing 2-player showdowns through multiway specifically to minimize this break. Rule: treat TableAction variant choices as part of end_hand's public contract; audit downstreams in the same PR.
